# Pipe Networks Pipe networks, commonly called pipenets, are a series of connected [textlink="pipes" link="Pipes"] that usually perform a common task.
Pipenets are used throughout the station to supply, remove, or otherwise transport gas. Good examples are the station's Distro and Wastenet, which supply breathable air and remove waste gases, respectively.
## How pipe networks work In Space Station 14, a pipenet behaves as a single defined volume with entry and exit points at the ends of the network. Forcing gas into or out of a pipenet with a [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"] affects the entire network, not just the pipe to which it is connected.
Pipenets are only separated by devices capable of interrupting flow or by certain special devices. For example, a [textlink="pressure pump" link="Pumps"] will not allow gas to pass through if it is unpowered or has nothing to pump.
Examples of devices that separate pipe networks include: - [textlink="Pressure and volume pumps" link="Pumps"] - [textlink="Gas mixers and filters" link="MixingAndFiltering"] - [textlink="All valves" link="Valves"] - [textlink="Radiators" link="Radiators"]
